assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn a defined enzymatic chemistry, cytidine and engineered adenosine deamination on DNA, into a programmable tool for single-nucleotide change without double-strand breaks. It is a clear case of chemical mechanism under a biological process, and it gives biologists a general tool and a route to treating point-mutation disease.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory is the decisive origin; Komor (cytosine editor) and Gaudelli (adenine editor, requiring evolved TadA) made the two founding molecular inventions. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were close in time and could complicate a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction is extensive and first clinical results exist, so the core claim is stable. Recognition is timely, though clinical benefit is still accumulating.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize may weigh on committee appetite.
Priority between Liu-lab and Kondo/Nishida work is not something I can verify here.
Long-term safety, including off-target deamination, is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, built on reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule detection, changed how genomes, transcriptomes and mutational spectra are measured. For genome-maintenance work it is indispensable, and it is a molecular chemistry invention at its core.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived the Solexa chemistry; Jingyue Ju (terminator chemistry), Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454) and Mayer (clustering) also have strong claims. The three-person limit forces a contested choice.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is overwhelming and global, and the technology is mature. If anything, recognition is late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit the chemistry or the instrument and platform.
Competing claims of Ju, Rothberg and Mayer are unresolved.
I am recalling patent and priority history from memory, not verifying it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved the chemical problem of encapsulating and delivering nucleic acids into cells, with pKa-tuned lipid chemistry as the key idea. They enabled siRNA therapy (patisiran) and mRNA vaccines at global scale, a very large demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the ionizable lipid concept and formulation; Anderson and Langer's lipidoid and combinatorial work, and MacLachlan, Hope and Madden in the lipid-particle lineage, all contributed. The attribution is genuinely diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Clinical and population-scale validation is exceptionally strong. The timing is very good given the 2023 Medicine prize for the mRNA modifications, but that also raises overlap concerns.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent Medicine recognition of the mRNA vaccine field.
Credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is hard to apportion.
Whether it is seen as chemistry or pharmaceutics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A modification defined an RNA chemical mark with writers, erasers (FTO, ALKBH5) and readers, tied to development, cancer and metabolism. It is a clear chemistry-of-life discovery and an epitranscriptomic counterpart to DNA methylation.
assessment.attribution: Rechavi and Jaffrey mapped m6A transcriptome-wide; He's laboratory identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and built the reader/writer framework. Jia, Yang, Dominissini and Meyer are important contributors, so the three-person selection is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Core findings are broadly reproduced, but some functional interpretations and single-nucleotide mapping methods have been revised. The field is still moving.
uncertainties: Disputed quantification and mapping specificity of m6A sites.
Limited therapeutic translation so far.
Possibly slightly early compared with more settled candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme that converts N2 to ammonia, and its structure (FeMo-cofactor with the interstitial carbide) and the radical-like electron-transfer mechanism are central metalloenzyme chemistry. I value the iron-sulfur and radical enzymology, which resembles RNR in spirit.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structure and cofactor work, Einsle identified the central carbide, Seefeldt and Dean built the mechanistic and genetic foundation, and Ribbe contributed cofactor biosynthesis. The credit is spread over several decades.
assessment.maturity: Structural facts are well confirmed; the catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction still has open intermediates, so the story is incomplete.
uncertainties: The N2-binding and reduction mechanism is not fully resolved.
The attribution across structural and mechanistic work is diffuse.
Late-career status of some pioneers is not something I can verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glues reframed drug action as induced proximity for degradation, an extension of ubiquitin-proteasome chemistry into a general design principle. Clinical candidates already exist.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structural design principles. The glue branch (Handa, Ito, Kim, Sakamoto, Gray) is partly distinct and the compound discovery may need separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Concept validated in many laboratories; approval of a degrader is still pending, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Whether PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues are one discovery or two.
Clinical benefit relative to inhibitors is unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate designed chemistry into proteins, giving a general tool for mechanism, probes and therapeutics. Originality and generality are high.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo incorporation systems in bacteria and eukaryotes; Chin extended to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Yokoyama and Mehl are also credited and the line between founders is not sharp.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and widely used; applications are mature in research, with fewer medical successes.
uncertainties: Competition from the intellectual lineage of Hecht, Furter and others is not in the list.
Efficiency limits in living organisms.
Medical impact is modest so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cryo-EM structures of the spliceosome showed how a huge RNA-protein machine arranges the two transesterification steps, giving a structural-chemical account of splicing catalysis by RNA.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann's group built the biochemical and structural framework; Shi's group gave key high-resolution yeast structures. Stark and Nguyen are additional contributors, so credit is shared.
assessment.maturity: Structures are mutually consistent across groups, though dynamics are still being worked out. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier splicing Medicine prize (1993) and ribozyme chemistry prizes.
Partial incompleteness of the mechanistic picture.
Fit with prior structural-biology prizes.
